questions.q: Driftwood's VP of Support asks, "Can you just show me how many tickets we're getting each day this month, broken down by priority?" What should happen next?
options: Ask follow-up questions to turn the vague request into a specific, answerable one
Open Snowflake and start writing a query immediately so there's something to show Monday
Tell the VP the request is too vague to act on
Build a full dbt project before touching the question, since that's the house standard
questions.explain: A short clarifying conversation up front prevents guessing wrong on scope, time window, or grain and finding out only after the deadline.

questions.q: Why does this beginner project deliberately skip dbt and Airflow, even though the Advanced Snowflake Data Engineering Capstone uses both?
options: This project has one stakeholder and one data source, which doesn't yet need a transformation framework or an orchestrator
dbt and Airflow don't work with Snowflake
Driftwood Media has never heard of dbt or Airflow
Beginner-tier courses are not allowed to mention other tools
questions.explain: Matching effort to the actual ask is part of scoping correctly — dbt and Airflow earn their place once there are multiple stakeholders and sources to coordinate, not before.

questions.q: What does 'grain' mean for this project's report?
options: The level of detail each row represents — here, one row per calendar day and priority combination
The Snowflake warehouse size needed to run the query
The number of support agents who touched a ticket
The file format used to load the ticket data
questions.explain: Grain describes how fine or coarse each result row is — here, each row is one day plus one priority level.

questions.q: Once clarified, which of these is the correctly scoped requirement for this project?
options: A report showing the count of support tickets created each day this month, broken out by priority, refreshable on demand, for the VP of Support
A real-time dashboard showing every support ticket field for the entire company
A machine learning model predicting which tickets will become Urgent
A one-time static export with no breakdown by priority
questions.explain: The clarified ask keeps the original request's intent — daily counts by priority, refreshable, for one stakeholder — without adding scope nobody asked for.

questions.q: Why does the VP's ask NOT need row-level masking or multi-role governance at this stage?
options: The report shows aggregate ticket counts by day and priority, not individual customer PII, for a single read-only stakeholder
Snowflake does not support masking policies
Masking is only needed once a project uses Airflow
The VP of Support is an administrator and sees everything anyway
questions.explain: A one-role, aggregate, read-only report is proportionate to the actual request — governance complexity should match the data and audience, not be added by default.
